entry: New: Move a point. In the skill tree, a new panel lets you swap one skill you own for another without a restart. It costs 1 knowledge on top of the price difference, and a skill that other skills depend on cannot be moved. Your lifetime knowledge total is unchanged.

New: a Halloween event, Night of Storms. From about 25 October to 1 November a banner offers a small task: finish one run with resources left. Doing it earns a Halloween badge that shows on your game page and on the hub. Nothing is lost if you skip it, and the badge is kept in your save.

New: run codes and challenges. After a run you can copy a short run code for a friend; paste a friend's code under Run codes and challenges to play the same events in the same order with your own skill tree and memory switched off, so you both start from a fresh settlement. A challenge earns no knowledge and leaves your history alone (it counts toward a Challenge runs finished tally), and the result is a friendly note rather than a ranking. Codes are not checked by a server.

New: a Schedule builder. Pick 3 to 7 events from the event library, reorder them, save the schedule by name, run it (your skill tree applies) and share a code for the schedule alone. Runs on a built schedule are tagged Custom schedule in Review Past Runs, never go on the hardest-schedule board, and earn knowledge in proportion to the damage the schedule throws compared with the Classic mix.

New: a difficulty-adjusted score. Every run now shows its raw score and an adjusted one, which asks how you would have done if every event had struck at the typical 1.00x severity (harsher draws are credited, gentler ones discounted). It appears in the run summary, Review Past Runs (which can also sort by it), the toughest run line, the toughest-run badge and the copied summary.

New: allocation presets. Name a set of units such as Flood plan: 3 resilience, 1 growth, then apply it in one click (U undoes it as one click); it buys what you can afford and stops at the 85% cap. Make them in the Allocation presets panel, which can fill the numbers from what you bought this turn.

New: a save health badge under Runs completed. It says Saved Ns ago, or warns in words when this browser's storage is full or blocked or the stored copy no longer matches this page, and then offers one click to export your progress code.

New in the skill tree: a search box and filter chips (Affordable, Pinned, Owned, and by type: Weather, Social, All events, Starting build), plus a Purchase route under your pinned skills that lists what to buy in order, prerequisites first, with a running knowledge total and an estimate of how many more runs it will take. Also: arrow keys move between skills, Enter unlocks and P pins; panels take keyboard focus when they open and give it back when they close; and the schedule is available as plain text.

New: a closing line on the run summary, chosen from a bank of 36 lines to match how the run went (a flawless defence, a surplus, a resilience-heavy or growth-heavy build, a steady run, plus a few place-specific lines). Lines for a hard run are kept gentle. You can hide it with the new Settings checkbox Hide the closing line on the run summary.

New: an improvement streak. When two or more runs in a row each beat your best score so far, a flame line under your run comparison says how many, and those runs get a flame and a warm glow in Review Past Runs (shown as an icon and words, not only colour).

Review Past Runs grew up: you can sort the list (newest, oldest, best or worst score, by scenario), show only standard, extended or one scenario's runs, archive runs you no longer want in the way (their score and knowledge still count), write a short note on any run (kept with your progress and included in the backup code), and tick two runs to see them side by side with the differences marked, including the damage of each event.

New setting: Ask before facing an event with unspent resources (off by default, in Settings and included in Reset to Default). When it is on, Face Next Event first asks whether you want to keep, say, 80 resources unspent, and tells you how much resilience or growth they could still buy; it only asks, it never changes a number, and it stays quiet when you cannot afford anything or the run is over.

New: after each event, a collapsible How that damage was worked out section shows the hit step by step: the base damage, what the severity added or took off, how much each protection took away (resilience, Early Warning, Mutual Aid, your category skill and any societal memory), the 85% cap when it bites, and the damage taken, as a stacked bar with every number also written as a line.

New: every locked skill in the tree now has a Helps against line. Early Warning, Mutual Aid, Climate Hardening and Civic Preparedness name which of the events still to come they would soften (for example Flood x2, Heatwave, Storm) and the exact damage they would save over the rest of this run at your current build, and the starting-build skills say how they help from your next run's first event.

New: a Schedule strip under the next-event line lists every event of the run as a small chip with its number, icon and name. Done events are ticked, the next one is marked with an arrow, and hovering or focusing any chip (it is also reachable with Tab) shows its details underneath: the exact damage you would take at your current build, its severity, your mitigation and any category bonus, so you can see how an investment changes the whole run.

New kind of shock: the Heat-Health Emergency, where a heat wave endangers people rather than buildings or supply lines. It belongs to a new health category (teal, with a thermometer) and arrives in the new Heat season scenario, picked before a run starts; the Classic mix and every older save are unchanged. The Disaster Codex gains a seventh page with the 1995 Chicago heat wave as its sourced real-world note, your settlement can carry a health scar, and two new achievements reward facing it and filling all seven pages. Seen It All still means the original six.

New: the run summary has a Copy result button that copies one line, such as Aftermath, 340 resources left, with your run, events weathered, damage taken and flawless defenses (it sits beside the existing Copy run summary, which still copies the full event-by-event text). Every achievement you have earned now has a Share button that copies a line you can paste anywhere, with the share of players who have it when that figure is available. The How to Play and Info panels link to the new Credits page.

New in Aftermath: a Disaster Codex (one page per kind of shock, filling in with your damage, best mitigation and a sourced real-world story as you face each one) and a Lifetime Stats page. Invest in steps of x1, x5 or Max, and undo your last investment click before Face Next Event. Hold an event to 15% of its base damage for a Flawless Defense (a bonus knowledge point and a new achievement), see how many knowledge points came from where, copy your run summary, and watch each hit's prevented damage and streak. The tab title tracks your run, events are announced for screen readers, and Settings gains High contrast and Readable font. Keys: 1 and 2 invest, Enter faces the event, U undoes, T jumps to the tree, H, C and S open History, Codex and Stats.

Desktop layout: on a wide window with a mouse, Aftermath can now open as a full-window dashboard. The settlement, the next event and your mitigation fill the main area, your Resources, Resilience, Growth and Knowledge sit in a strip of chips across the top, and the investments, Face Next Event and the skill tree stay in a column on the right. History, community, backup and the other panels open as windows from the Menu (or press Escape). Same saves as the Classic layout, which is unchanged; switch from the opening screen or the Menu.

Light theme polish: the four status pills no longer stay near-black under dark text, the Face Next Event button and the weather, non-weather and social event colours were deepened for readable contrast, and dimmed captions were darkened. The event hues are kept. Dark mode is unchanged (Y11b).

In the real world: a collapsible note beside the run showing one real recovery or response for the kind of shock you last faced (Room for the River, France's heat plan, Bangladesh's cyclone volunteers, the Suez blockage, the 2003 blackout, Christchurch's student volunteers), each with its source linked (W2).

Real places: the scenario picker gains San Francisco, Houston, Phoenix and Chicago, each a simplified mapping of that place's best-known hazards onto the game's event types (San Francisco: earthquake and wildfire risk, no storms; Houston: hurricanes and floods; Phoenix: heat; Chicago: storms and heat) (E17b).
Community resilience index: a line under the settlement showing the average number of resilience skills unlocked across all players (E9).
Community leaderboard: an opt-in 'hardest schedule survived' board ranked by the average event severity of a run you came through with resources left (E23).
Resilience curriculum: a guided sequence of five runs, each with one goal that teaches one idea, done in order (E19).
Resilience mentor: an optional inline suggestion, right where you decide, that reads your run and says what it would do and why (E27).
Societal memory: a run that ends in ruin leaves a permanent, unique defence against the kind of shock that broke it (E29).
Climate scenario pack: pick a Coastal, Inland or Urban schedule (or the Classic mix) before a run's first event or between runs (E17a).
Achievement cards now show "Earned by N% of players" once enough real save data exists for that achievement (site-wide goal, Z1/Z27b).
Added a keyboard-shortcuts help overlay: press ? to see it, Esc to close it or whichever panel is open (site-wide goal, Z4).
Settings panel: added a "Reset to Default" button that resets text size and reduce-motion back to their defaults in one click (site-wide goal, folded from A26).

The end-of-run summary is now print-friendly: printing the page (e.g. Ctrl/Cmd+P) while it's open hides the site chrome and renders it in clean dark-on-white, instead of the site's usual dark theme and UI.
Reset Skill Tree now uses the site's shared confirmation dialog (with the exact refund amount in its message) instead of a click-twice button.

The settlement's ground now visibly scars where it's been hit before — a small crack for each of weather, infrastructure, and social shocks, deepening the more times you've weathered that kind of disaster across every run.
Fixed a bug where the Achievements and What's New panels showed as empty boxes before first use, and stayed visible forever after being closed once — a missing CSS override for the hidden state.

Toolbar cleanup: Info Page/Achievements/Past Runs/Changelog moved out of a stranded second toolbar into the main one at the top, next to Tutorial/How to Play, with Settings last — matching every other game's layout (site-wide Z12 audit).

Round-2 pass: two new skill branches (weather hardening, civic preparedness against social shocks), a settlement name and always-visible runs counter, pin-a-skill runs-until-affordable estimates, expected-damage ranges, severity tooltips, one-time reassurance callouts, past-run memories in event flavor, extended-run epilogue, and build-diversity achievements.
Added a settings panel (text size + reduced motion) and completed a colorblind-safety audit — no color-only state found needing a fix.

Achievements system added (19 achievements, unlock toast, hub dashboard link) plus a large backlog pass: new skill nodes, expanded legacy history, past-run review, export/import codes, and extended-run mode.
Added a skippable tutorial, a How to Play page, and a mobile sticky HUD.
Full visual redesign: space-themed backdrop, glass panels, icon labels and stat chips.
Integrated the shared save widget and fixed a stale-save exploit that could double-award knowledge points on reload.
Pass 3 balance fix: event severity now widens with skill-tree strength, so a maxed-out run still has to react to something.
Added an in-game Info Page with real-world adaptation sources; Pass 2 added diversified event types and a settlement legacy system.
Iteration pass: deterministic per-run severity variation and real-practice grounding text on each skill unlock.
All 7 core milestones shipped: scheduled-event run loop, skill-tree currency, persistent skill tree, run-1-vs-latest hope-angle comparison, feedback prompt, and hub integration.
